the ported hunks rewrote the #include lines of 7 upstream-only board DTS (mt6755-evb.dts, mt6795-evb.dts, mt6797-evb.dts, mt6797-x20-dev.dts, mt2712e.dtsi, ...) to downstream-only paths, breaking 17 of 521 DTB builds. this sandbox has no OpenSSL, and CONFIG_SYSTEM_TRUSTED_KEYRING=y makes certs/Makefile run scripts/extract-cert with the (empty) key list. A stand-in implementing exactly that one case was compiled into the build object tree as the gitignored artifact kbuild would have produced; it exits non-zero for any non-empty key list so it can never silently mis-build a trust chain, and no file in the kernel source tree was patched.

items.action: revert the vendor power-on/nvram RTC rework to mainline (patch 0073)
items.reason: the ported hunks reference 4.19-only members (spare[], pm_nb, nvmem_cfg) and rtc_set_alarm_poweron(), which 5.15's include/linux/mfd/mt6397/core.h and mt6397-core.c do not provide. Caught only by enabling the driver from the built DTB - invisible through 24 build passes with the symbol off.

items.action: satisfy polling_rdma_output_line_is_not_zero() with a __weak no-op instead of deleting the call or disabling MTCMOS
items.reason: the vendor defines it in the display driver (drivers/misc/mediatek/video/mt6768/dispsys/ddp_rdma_ex.c:1588) as a wait on DISP_RDMA_OUT_LINE_CNT before an mm_sel re-parent on a command-mode panel; the video subtree is not ported, so the symbol is undefined at link. mm_polling() is already gated on subsys_is_on(SYS_DIS), so with no display driver bound there is no RDMA in flight to wait for; MT_MTCMOS_ENABLE=0 (the vendor's bringup config) would have discarded the file's purpose. The display port's strong definition overrides the stub. Stated loss if display lands without restoring the link: transient panel underflow on mid-frame mm_sel switches.

items.action: rename the header guard to __DRV_CLK_MTK_V1_H when transplanting
items.reason: 5.15's drivers/clk/mediatek/clk-mtk.h uses the guard __DRV_CLK_MTK_H that this vendor header also claims, and clk-mt6768-pg.c includes both; with the original guard whichever came first silently swallowed the other, which would have looked like a compile error in whichever header lost.

items.action: do not port the vendor legacy clock manager (nor clkdbg/clkchk)
items.reason: it is the pre-CCF manager that COMMON_CLK_MT6768 replaces and it registers the same DT nodes; porting both would give two providers per node. clk-mt6768.c references none of those files, so dropping them is not a semantic loss for the CCF path - but it is why the BSP's pericfg clock gating (which lived in clkmgr/clkbuf, not in DT phandles) has no 5.15 counterpart, recorded as the peri_clks gap.

items.action: audit clock enablement by resolving the DTB's flat clock cells against the driver's registered IDs, per provider domain
items.reason: 'the driver compiles and the symbol is on' says nothing about whether the provider can answer the board. Three tool bugs had to be fixed to make the number trustworthy, each of which would have produced a false all-clear or a false alarm: dtc -O dts prefixes nodes with their label ('pericfg: pericfg@10003000 {'), so a name-only regex lost the providers and made every reference look dangling; '#clock-cells' needs '#' in the property regex; multi-string compatibles print as one quoted string separated by \0 and must be split. Domain attribution also has to include mux/divider/factor tables, not just *_clks[], or topckgen reads as 5/65 registered when it is 65/65.
